pending_articles.title: When neuroscience meets machine learning: a taxonomic scoping review of machine and statistical learning approaches in sub-Saharan Africa
pending_articles.content: In high-resource economies, computational neuroscience research frequently employs machine learning (ML) and statistical learning (SL) techniques. While these methods provide effective ways to analyse multimodal, high-dimensional, and complex data they are underexplored in low resource settings. This taxonomic scoping review uses a systematic methodological approach to synthesise the application of ML and SL techniques in neuroscience research in sub-Saharan Africa. In addition to discussing findings, strengths, limitations, and future prospects, the work classifies current research by neuroscience domains, applications, learning tasks, datasets, tools, and techniques. In order for African researchers to contribute to and benefit from the global computational neuroscience landscape, our review contends that low- and middle-income countries must create and augment context-specific and representative datasets and incorporate appropriate features for model training. Future studies should focus on pragmatic rather than complex modelling, external validation, reproducibility, interpretability, and utilise real-world data to determine clinical utility.

pending_articles.title: Coordination without command: active inference and the route to embodied intelligence
pending_articles.content: Embodied intelligence depends on bodies whose contact with the environment, distribution of load and capacity for action are only partly known and are changed by movement. We argue that this creates a practical reason to organize inference through distributed, hierarchical and plural processes, using active inference to relate local belief updating, contextual constraints and action selection within a common framework. The proposal brings together established ideas from factorized inference, distributed control and embodied robotics, distinguishing their mathematical description from the location of computation and authority over action. The octopus provides biological motivation through its combination of peripheral sensorimotor processing and central influences on behavior, while an articulated hexapod illustrates selected architectural choices through six leg-local predictive controllers coupled by neighbor messages and a shared mechanical body. The simulation includes intact locomotion and movement following programmed limb withdrawal and graph reconfiguration, although these observations do not isolate the contribution of inference or establish remapping. Together, the biological example and computational illustration clarify how local inferential processes may remain coordinated across bodily interfaces and timescales without a controller prescribing the complete joint trajectory.

recently_processed.title: NOTCH3 p.R544C Drives Early Neurovascular Unit Dysfunction through Blood-Brain Barrier Failure, Complement Signalling and Metabolic Dysregulation
recently_processed.content: Cerebral small vessel disease is a major cause of stroke and vascular cognitive impairment, yet the mechanisms that initiate neurovascular dysfunction before irreversible brain injury remain poorly defined. CADASIL, caused by cysteine-altering NOTCH3 mutations, provides a genetically tractable model to resolve these early events. Here, we investigated the Asian-enriched NOTCH3 p.R544C variant and tested whether early disease emerges through interconnected blood-brain barrier (BBB), inflammatory, and metabolic dysfunction. NOTCH3 p.R544C iPSC-derived endothelial cells showed impaired angiogenesis and migration, reduced barrier resistance, disrupted tight-junction organisation, and altered vascular, adhesion, and extracellular-matrix programmes. In multicellular BBB-like microtissues, these defects propagated across the neurovascular unit, producing disorganised vascular networks, enlarged luminal structures, and increased permeability, establishing BBB failure as an early disease layer. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed coordinated loss of endothelial BBB transport and efflux programmes with astrocytic complement, innate immune, and matrix-remodelling activation. Secretome profiling and patient-plasma measurements converged on complement- and matrix-associated mediators, including C1S and CLU, identifying complement-matrix activation as a second interconnected layer. Importantly, combined cilostazol and isosorbide mononitrate treatment improved barrier function and reduced selected complement- and matrix-associated proteins in mutant microtissues, supporting pharmacological reversibility of components of this early disease programme. Seahorse analysis further demonstrated reduced mitochondrial respiratory capacity associated with NOTCH3 p.R544C. In vivo, three-month-old mutant mice showed altered cerebral pyruvate metabolism and early microvascular abnormalities, whereas six-month-old mice developed more prominent extracellular-matrix, inflammatory, and gliovascular changes, supporting an age-dependent transition from early metabolic dysregulation to broader neurovascular remodelling. Together, these findings define NOTCH3 p.R544C CADASIL as an early multicellular neurovascular disorder organised across three interconnected mechanistic layers: BBB failure, complement-matrix signalling, and metabolic dysregulation, while identifying early BBB-centred dysfunction as a potentially tractable state before advanced cerebrovascular injury develops.

recently_processed.title: Retinal Vessel Volume Density and Intraoperative Cortical Vascular Phenotypes in Moyamoya Disease
recently_processed.content: Background Angiographic staging describes large-artery stenosis and collateral evolution in moyamoya disease but does not directly depict the cortical surface vasculature, which can vary among patients with similar Suzuki stages. We examined whether a side-matched three-dimensional retinal vascular measure was associated with intraoperative cortical vascular phenotypes after accounting for Suzuki stage. Methods This prospective single-center cohort included 52 patients with moyamoya disease who underwent combined direct and indirect revascularization; 48 had analyzable retinal vessel volume density (RVVD) in the side-matched eye. RVVD was defined as the percentage of the corresponding retinal tissue volume occupied by three-dimensional optical coherence tomography angiography vascular signal within the central 6 x 6-mm region from the retinal nerve fiber layer to the inner plexiform layer. After dural opening and before vascular manipulation, overall cortical vascular richness and arterial, venous, and small-vessel richness were graded from 0 to 3. Associations were evaluated with Spearman correlation and proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and ipsilateral Suzuki stage. Results Mean RVVD was 12.92% (SD, 3.30 percentage points). Higher RVVD was associated with greater overall cortical vascular richness ({rho} =0.523; bias-corrected and accelerated bootstrap 95% CI, 0.279-0.714; P<0.001) and arterial richness ({rho} =0.522; 95% CI, 0.261-0.714; P<0.001). Per 1-SD higher RVVD, the adjusted cumulative odds ratio for being in a higher richness category was 3.92 (95% CI, 1.82-8.44; P<0.001) for overall cortical vascular richness and 4.31 (95% CI, 1.92-9.70; P<0.001) for arterial richness. Conclusions In moyamoya disease, higher side-matched RVVD was associated with richer overall and arterial cortical vascular phenotypes at revascularization surgery, independent of Suzuki stage. Three-dimensional retinal vascular imaging may therefore provide a noninvasive, side-specific preoperative measure of cortical vascular remodeling.
